name: AL-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's strong Republican lean (R+17 partisan baseline)
Jerry Carl's large fundraising and outside-spending edge over Clyde Jones Jr.
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at only about 3%
Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot and no public polling
model.rationale: The fundamentals point decisively Republican in this post-redistricting Gulf Coast seat, and Carl's roughly 13-to-1 fundraising advantage plus heavy outside support reinforce that picture. Markets and the district's lean leave little room for an upset, so the forecast sits near the fundamentals-based estimate with a slight Republican tilt beyond it.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal, a strong third-party or write-in dynamic, or a sudden influx of Democratic outside spending could narrow what is otherwise a lopsided race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 1st District is an open seat after redistricting drew incumbent lines together, and Republican Jerry Carl faces Democrat Clyde Jones Jr. in November. The district sits about seventeen points to the right of the nation, giving the Republican nominee a substantial structural advantage in any general election.

Carl has raised roughly $1.16 million with about $367,000 on hand, supplemented by more than half a million dollars in outside support, while Jones has raised under $90,000. Prediction markets give the Democrat only about a three percent chance of winning. With no public polling available, the race rests on fundamentals, and those fundamentals point clearly toward a Republican hold.
